[Lähde: The Guardian World]
EU’s Maroš Šefčovič says summit will ‘probably’ be in July but sources say it could be put back as talks deadlocked

The EU has said Keir Starmer’s upcoming summit “resetting” the UK-Europe relationship may still happen in July, amid growing fears it could be postponed to the autumn as talks over youth mobility remain deadlocked.

“The summit is supposed to be mid-July but at the moment it could be put back to after the summer,” said one EU diplomat.

“There is common concern that momentum is being lost. Negotiations always continue until the moment the clock stops and then you have a text the next morning, but because there is no deadline, the pressure is off,” the source added.

Speaking at a conference in Brussels, the EU trade commissioner, Maroš Šefčovič, said: “I believe that still the expectation is that we would have the summit, most probably in July.”

Asked if talks were deadlocked on a scheme to allow under-30s to travel freely on a three-year visa scheme for youth, he said it was one of the top three issues, and one that EU ministers cared deeply about.

Describing a recent meeting of 27 European ministers, he said: “When we were discussing the relationship with the UK, 20 ministers took the floor and said how the youth experience is important for them. So I think this is something what I see as an investment into the future.”

Šefčovič added that his second daughter studied in the UK, “she has all the university friends from there, she speaks much better English than I do, she can do the British accent excellently”.

His personal interest is reflected widely around governments in Europe, meaning it is turning into something of a red line for EU leaders.

The UK business secretary, Peter Kyle, who had an hour-long meeting with Šefčovič in Brussels on Friday, said: “We are very aware of the strength of feeling” about youth mobility but a deal had to be “respectful” for both sides.

The annual summit, the second of its kind since Brexit, was originally due to be held in May, exactly a year after the first, when Starmer and the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, met in Lancaster House in Westminster.

But with talks over a youth experience scheme and a veterinary deal taking longer than anticipated, 29 June was pencilled in for this year’s summit, according to sources.

That has now shifted to a tentative date of 13 July and there is speculation it may move again.

On June 23 2016, a majority of Britons chose to leave the European Union after a referendum campaign driven by the promises of supporters of the “Leave” camp, spearheaded by Nigel Farage and Boris Johnson. Built around the slogan “Take Back Control”, the pro-Brexit campaign promised to restore the country’s sovereignty, regain control over migration flows, and boost economic prosperity. Ten years on, hopes have given way to a bitter sense of disillusion that the British refer to as “Bregret”, and it is a divided, weakened, disenchanted country who is about to commemorate the tenth anniversary of the referendum.

There are few events in a country’s national history that constitute such an immense and profound shock as Brexit. The announcement of the results, that indicated a 51.9% victory for the “Leave” camp, sent shockwaves across the world. After 43 years of a relationship that was often turbulent and confrontational, the United Kingdom decided to leave the European Union and open a new chapter in its history.

The reasons for the shock were manifold: first, it was an unprecedented event that raised many uncertainties and fears about the future of the United Kingdom and the European Union alike; the shock was also explained by the completely unexpected nature of the victory, given that the main polling institutes were predicting a close election, giving the “Remain” camp a slight edge; finally, the vote in favour of Brexit represented a political and ideological victory for Nigel Farage, the then leader of the far right populist United Kingdom Independence Party (UKIP) which was fiercely hostile to the European Union, immigration and multiculturalism.

Previously considered more of an outsider, Nigel Farage then went on to become a central figure in the British political landscape, unanimously recognised as the main architect of Brexit. His campaign themes – which revolved primarily around the fight against immigration, restoring national sovereignty, and defending British national identity – emerged as the dominant themes in the national debate. payload.title: Britannian ja EU:n suhteiden elvytyshuippukokous saattaa yhä toteutua heinäkuussa
payload.summary: EU:n kauppakomissaari Maroš Šefčovič arvioi, että Britannian ja EU:n suhteita käsittelevä huippukokous pidetään todennäköisesti heinäkuussa, vaikka neuvottelujen etenemisestä on herännyt epävarmuutta.
payload.content:
EU:n kauppakomissaari Maroš Šefčovič on sanonut, että Britannian ja EU:n suhteiden uutta vaihetta käsittelevä huippukokous on yhä odotettavissa todennäköisesti heinäkuussa. Taustalla on kuitenkin epäilyjä mahdollisesta viivästymisestä, sillä neuvottelut ovat jumiutuneet erityisesti nuorten liikkuvuutta koskevan järjestelyn ympärille.

## Heinäkuu on yhä esillä

Britannian pääministeri Keir Starmerin hallinto on hakenut suhteisiin EU:n kanssa uutta alkua brexitin jälkeisten vuosien jälkeen. Huippukokouksen ajankohdaksi oli lähdetietojen mukaan ensin kaavailtu 29. kesäkuuta, mutta suunnitelma on sittemmin siirtynyt alustavasti 13. heinäkuuta. Lähteiden mukaan myös uusi siirto on mahdollinen.

Šefčovič sanoi Brysselissä järjestetyssä konferenssissa uskovansa, että odotus on edelleen huippukokouksen pitäminen todennäköisesti heinäkuussa. Samalla EU-diplomaattien piirissä on arvioitu, että kokous voisi siirtyä kesän jälkeiseen aikaan, jos sopua ei löydy riittävän nopeasti.

Erään EU-diplomaatin mukaan yhteinen huoli liittyy siihen, että neuvottelujen vauhti on hiipumassa. Lähteen mukaan neuvotteluissa voidaan usein edetä viime hetkellä, mutta selkeän määräajan puute vähentää painetta saada teksti valmiiksi.

## Nuorten liikkuvuus on keskeinen kiistakohta

Keskeiseksi kysymykseksi on noussut nuorten liikkuvuutta koskeva malli. Esillä on järjestely, joka antaisi alle 30-vuotiaille mahdollisuuden matkustaa vapaammin kolmen vuoden viisumijärjestelyn puitteissa. Šefčovičin mukaan asia kuuluu kolmen tärkeimmän neuvottelukysymyksen joukkoon ja on monille EU-ministereille erityisen tärkeä.

Šefčovič kuvasi EU-maiden ministerien tuoretta keskustelua niin, että 20 ministeriä 27:stä käytti puheenvuoron Britannia-suhteesta ja korosti nuorten kokemusten merkitystä. Hänen mukaansa kyse on tulevaisuuteen tehtävästä investoinnista.

## Neuvotteluissa on muitakin avoimia asioita

Neuvotteluja hidastavat nuorten liikkuvuusjärjestelyn rinnalla myös eläinlääkintäalan sopimukseen liittyvät kysymykset. Käytettävissä olevien lähdetietojen mukaan niiden käsittely on vienyt odotettua enemmän aikaa. Britannian puolelta Kyle kuvasi tapaamistaan Šefčovičin kanssa myönteiseksi, mutta lähdekatkelmat eivät osoita, että ratkaiseva läpimurto olisi jo saavutettu.

Neuvotteluja hidastavat erityisesti nuorten liikkuvuusjärjestely ja eläinlääkintäsopimus.

EU’s Maroš Šefčovič says summit will ‘probably’ be in July but sources say it could be put back as talks deadlocked The EU has said Keir Starmer’s upcoming summit “resetting” the UK-Europe relationship may still happen in July, amid growing fears it could be postponed to the autumn as talks over youth mobility remain deadlocked. “The summit is supposed to be mid-July but at the moment it could be put back to after the summer,” said one EU diplomat. “There is common concern that momentum is being lost. Negotiations always continue until the moment the clock stops and then you have a text the next morning, but because there is no deadline, the pressure is off,” the source added.

Speaking at a conference in Brussels, the EU trade commissioner, Maroš Šefčovič, said: “I believe that still the expectation is that we would have the summit, most probably in July.” Asked if talks were deadlocked on a scheme to allow under-30s to travel freely on a three-year visa scheme for youth, he said it was one of the top three issues, and one that EU ministers cared deeply about. Describing a recent meeting of 27 European ministers, he said: “When we were discussing the relationship with the UK, 20 ministers took the floor and said how the youth experience is important for them. So I think this is something what I see as an investment into the future.”

But with talks over a youth experience scheme and a veterinary deal taking longer than anticipated, 29 June was pencilled in for this year’s summit, according to sources.
